decision: Keep stochastic9 experimental and disabled by default. It is a different spatial kernel plus stochastic estimation; the native TSR leaves more same-phase static noise and light-step response does not improve.
caveats: Static final/source RMS ratio compares the same linear HDR luma units. Raw shadow visibility RMS is separate.
Reference is 8 jitter phases of the same 2048-resolution disk kernel with 1024 comparisons, not higher-resolution visibility truth.
Light settle criterion is first run of 3 consecutive Active frames with absolute old-state projection retention below 10%; not proof every pixel is settled or all later frames stay below threshold.
Each light-step variant has one VSM fallback frame at step16. Response summaries start at Active step17.
Camera moving-frame differences include geometric change, kernel change and stochastic variation; no ghosting claim is made from them.
Camera post-motion same-phase residual includes recovery; even tent source differs from the separately warmed static stage, so static-baseline output error is not exclusively TSR error.
No performance conclusion from diagnostic capture.
next_tsr_validation: Using unchanged raw shadows, A/B a lighting-change rejection trigger independent of receiver motion, with a threshold robust against stochastic noise. Keep depth rejection independent in diagnosis.

Instrument current color, pre/post-AABB-clipped history, normalized luma/chroma change, chosen history weight and resurrection validity/weight. A color rejection can still resurrect old color through TSRUpdateHistory.

Repeat the identical phase-aligned light-step and static fixtures. Require lower old-state response delay while checking common-edge static variance, rejection rate and aliasing, rather than optimizing acceptance alone.
Add a slower continuous moving-shadow fixture after the step result passes; retain raw-source/final distinction and separate VSM invalidation from TSR response.
